title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with the organizer’s actual attendee location and daily finish time — ticket-holder access to the Thunderpick Finals is still unconfirmed. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates between Qawra and Ta’ Qali, not confirmed hotel-to-entrance journeys. One thing is now settled from the operator’s own timetable: Route 186 is asymmetric, serving Il-Qawra only toward Ta’ Qali, while its return terminates at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527), so a return to AX ODYCY always needs a second boarding and its last listed departure from Ta’ Qali Stadium 2194 is 20:53. Malta Public Transport’s published fares were read directly on 11 October 2026 (single day-route journeys €2.50 in the summer window / €2.00 in winter, €3.00 night and Tallinja Direct, €3.50 on TD1, €19 for 12 journeys, €25 for the 7-day Explore Adult card, €27 for the 7-day Explore Flex), and travel cards can be bought at the Buġibba Terminal. Use the date-specific planner for both directions and keep a live-quote taxi fallback — on 17 October that fallback is the primary plan, because a published evening diversion removes part of the return chain and a large ticketed event runs in the same area from 22:00.

records.name: Thunderpick World Championship 2026 — dates, venue and confirmed address
records.address: Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre (MFCC), South Gate National Stadium, Ta’ Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard, Malta
records.hours: Official phase dates: arrival 12 October; media day 13 October; Group Stage 14–16 October; Playoffs 17–18 October; departure 19 October 2026. Public door times for these TWC dates are not published.
records.description: The official Thunderpick page confirms the phase dates and gives Malta as the location. A Thunderpick release names BLAST Studios Malta as the host venue, and BLAST’s own attendee guide for a separate event at the same studio lists the venue as the Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre, Ta Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard. The VisitMalta business directory lists “BLAST Arena Studios Malta” at MFCC South Gate National Stadium, Attard ATD 4000, and the 16 September 2026 Thunderpick release is datelined Ta’ Qali, Malta. The venue identity and postal address are therefore corroborated by the operator, the venue operator’s own guest guide and the national tourism authority. What is still NOT published for this event is the attendee ticket status, the public entrance/gate to use, and the daily doors or match times.

Naming release (VALLETTA dateline): https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thunderpick-world-championship-2026-returns-to-malta-with-1-million-prize-pool-302850221.html . records.name: Qawra ↔ Ta’ Qali Stadium — Route 186 (direct bus to the event area)
records.address: Operator stop sequence read end-to-end on 11 October 2026. TOWARD TA' QALI / RABAT: Buġibba Bay 6 (3531) → Ben (949) → Il-Qawra Arznell (950) → Luzzu (951) → Qawra (952) → Boxxla (953) → Fugass (954) → Wileg (955) → Burmarrad → Mosta (Targa 1138, Rotunda 4 2565, Bezzina 1102, Gholja 1/2) → Ta' Qali Stadium (6227) → Villagg (6228) → Snajja (2191) → Rabat (Rabat 4 2567). RETURN TOWARD BUĠIBBA: Rabat 2 (2569) → Mdina (135) → Saqqajja (4627) → Ta' Qali Stadium (2194) → Ħ'Attard → Mosta → Burmarrad → St Paul's Bay → Buġibba Moll (6193) → Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) TERMINUS. The return direction lists no Il-Qawra stop. Verify stop sides, safe walks and the onward hotel connection in the dated planner.
records.hours: Operator timetable read 11 October 2026 on a repeating 30-minute pattern. Toward Ta' Qali: Qawra 952 first 06:09–06:10, last 21:38–21:39; Ta' Qali Stadium 6227 first 06:34–06:43, last 22:03–22:08 depending on the variant, about 25–33 minutes after the Qawra times within the same run; Il-Qawra stops served roughly 06:08–21:39. RETURN: Stadium 2194 first 05:52, LAST LISTED 20:53; terminus Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) last listed 21:26–21:36 depending on the variant, about 33 minutes after Stadium 2194. The extracted page carries several timetable variants without reliable day-type context, so treat these as static-grid spans rather than trip-day guarantees and confirm the date-specific departure in the operator's planner.
records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is the only route in the operator's tables that links Qawra's seafront stops directly to the Ta' Qali stadium stop, but it is ASYMMETRIC and that is the single most important transport fact for this trip. Traced stop by stop on 11 October 2026, the direction that serves Il-Qawra (Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952) runs toward Ta' Qali and Rabat, while the return from opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 lists NO Il-Qawra stop at all and terminates at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). A return to AX ODYCY on Route 186 therefore always means alighting in the Buġibba area and boarding a second service toward Qawra, and the last listed return departure from Stadium 2194 is 20:53 — the binding constraint for a late playoff finish. One single fare covers both legs because onboard tickets are valid two hours with free transfers. These are published static departure grids for the current timetable, not a saved date-specific journey; the walk from stop 6227 or 2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate has not been measured, and the onward Buġibba → Qawra connection must come from the dated planner rather than be inferred from the operator's stop lists.
records.notes: Operator route page with the stop-by-stop grids, read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Stops confirmed in that page’s lists: Il-Qawra Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952, Ta’ Qali Gibjun 6118, Venture 6226, Stadium 6227 and Villagg 6228; Rabat 4 (2567) is the other terminus. The same page shows stops 6227/6228/2191 also served by Routes 56 and 202, and the Stadium 6227 stop is also listed for the Ta’ Qali Park & Ride shuttles 403, 404 and 405 — useful alternates to compare in the planner. Route 214 lists Qawra and Qali-area stops as a second option: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ . For the Saturday 17 October evening diversion see the separate diversion record. Date-specific planner (not run here): https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . The operator’s public notice of the 17 October diversion is at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Second-session caveats (11 October 2026): the static page shows multiple time variants and earlier tighter bounds were withdrawn rather than presented as trip-day times; the date-specific planner is https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Return stop 2194 was independently re-read on 11 October; outbound 6227 and return 2194 are different direction stops, so no single clock range is asserted. Route 186 is a day route, so a single journey costs the day-route price and is covered by the 7-day Explore Adult card; the closest listed sales office to Qawra is the Buġibba Terminal: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . Third-pass additions (11 October 2026): the full return chain toward Buġibba was traced stop by stop and contains no Il-Qawra stop — Rabat 2 (2569), Mdina (135), Saqqajja (4627), Qanpiena (2232), Telgha (2231), Snajja (2192), Villagg (2193), Stadium (2194), Venture (6134), Gibjun (4125), Ħ'Attard Sedqa (2457), Marg (2458), Gheneb (5674), Mosta Waqqafa (2196), Trincetta (2200), Gholja 2 (1101), Mithna (1099), Milt (1097), Gatt (1143), Kungress (1142), Rotunda 2 (2563), Isouard (1105), Kostituzzjoni (1106), Targa (1107), Gharusa (1200), Rihana (1202), Campra (1203), Ramez (1204), Burmarrad (1205), Qannotta (1206), Qadi (1207), Mwiezeb (956), Imhasel (958), Toni (6013), Gillieru (6014), Moll (6193), Rizzi (946), Sajf (947), Gzejjer (948), Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). records.name: Route 186 diversion and the wider Ta' Qali / Mosta evening detour cluster — 17–18 October
records.address: Route 186 toward Buġibba; affected stops listed by MPT are Gholja 2 through Targa
records.hours: Weekly on Friday and Saturday, 19:00–00:00, starting 17 October 2026 and ending 18 October 2026 at approximately 00:00
records.description: Malta Public Transport publishes a Route 186 diversion effective weekly on Fridays and Saturdays from 19:00 to 00:00, starting 17 October and ending 18 October at approximately 00:00, stating that toward Buġibba the stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served. Because 17 October is a Playoffs day and the notice names only those intermediate stops, it does not by itself say whether a Ta' Qali Stadium departure or a Qawra-ward connection is cancelled — but the omitted segment is precisely the stretch between Ta' Qali and Buġibba that the last listed 20:53 return uses, so a post-event bus return that evening may not run as the static grid shows. The same service-updates page lists a CLUSTER of further detours on the identical Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 pattern from 17 October affecting Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 in the Mosta, Rotunda and Ta' Qali P&R area — including Route 405 omitting Rotunda 1 and Bezzina toward Mosta/Ta' Qali P&R and Route 47 omitting Gatt through Rotunda 1 toward Mosta. A large open-air event is ticketed at UNO Malta in Ta' Qali, Attard from 22:00 on Saturday 17 October, which is consistent with that cluster, but MPT names no cause and none is asserted here. The page also carries a separate, longer-running weekly Friday/Saturday 20:00–00:00 detour ending 21 April with the same affected-stop wording, so the operator is publishing overlapping notices and the live planner is authoritative on the day. Treat the whole Ta' Qali bus corridor as unreliable after 19:00 on 17 October and plan a taxi or ride-hailing return.
records.notes: Read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ under “Latest Service Updates”: a detour weekly on Friday and Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October, ending 18 October at about 00:00, “Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served”; and a second notice weekly on Friday and Saturday 20:00–00:00 ending 21 April with identical affected-stop wording. The same page also lists a stop closure at Saqqajja (ID 4627) on Routes 109, 109A, 181, 182, 186, 201, 202, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56 and N52, ends 1 January approximately 04:00, and Tuesday 13 October 09:30–17:30 construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. All-service-updates page: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Do not infer a cancelled or extra TWC service from these notices. The notice specifies affected stops rather than a total cancellation of Route 186, and it does not itself confirm whether a particular post-event bus will serve the required Qawra stop. Also listed on the operator’s service-updates page on 11 October 2026: Tuesday 13 October (09:30–17:30) construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. Recheck the operator’s updates and planner on the day. Third-pass addition (11 October 2026), read on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ : the wider Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 cluster from 17 October covers Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 around Mosta, Rotunda and Ta' Qali P&R. MPT states no cause for the cluster; the UNO Malta event is recorded separately in data/activities.json from the official ticketing platform and is NOT presented as the operator's stated reason. The Route 186 notice wording is: "Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served."

records.name: Malta Airport ↔ Qawra by Airport Direct TD1 (Il-Qawra stop Arznell 950)
records.area: Malta International Airport ↔ Qawra / Buġibba / north Malta
records.address: Airport bus terminal (Airport 1 stop 2550 outbound; Airport 3 stop 2552 return) ↔ Il-Qawra stop Arznell (ID 950) and Buġibba stops Sajf (947), Bugibba Bay 8 (2339), and Wileg (955). Confirm the stop nearest the hotel entrance in the planner.
records.hours: MPT’s Route TD1 timetable (read 11 Oct 2026) lists hourly departures from Airport 1 (stop 2550) on the hour from 05:00 to 00:00, reaching Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) at 05:42–00:35; return departures toward Airport 3 (stop 2552) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) hourly at 05:28–23:26 on weekdays and 05:27–23:27 on weekends.
records.description: This is the most straightforward published public-bus option from Malta International Airport toward Qawra: Airport Direct TD1 runs from the airport toward Ċirkewwa via Buġibba and the Qawra area, and its operator timetable confirms service at Il-Qawra stop Arznell (ID 950) in both directions. The airport terminal is signposted from arrivals. Buses have luggage space; no advance booking is required. The precise walk from stop Arznell 950 to AX ODYCY was not independently measured.
records.notes: Route stop and times: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TD1/. MPT also lists TD5 Airport Direct toward Rabat/Buġibba hourly at €3; its Qawra suitability was not established here. Operator information and fares: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/. Independently re-read 11 October (chunks 7–9): both the Airport 1 outbound sequence (05:42–00:35 at Arznell 950) and the Ċirkewwa-to-Airport 3 return sequence (05:28–23:26 weekday / 05:27–23:27 weekend at Arznell 950) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell 950. This supports route-level Qawra service in both directions, while the hotel walk and flight-specific departure still require a journey-planner check. Fare context re-verified 11 October 2026 against the operator’s own table, which lists Tallinja Direct routes at €3.00 and TD1 at €3.50: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . The same page states that the 7-day Explore Adult card excludes tallinja Direct routes, while the 12 Single Day Journeys card may be used on the Airport Direct service at a cost of two journeys per trip.

records.name: Bus fares, travel cards and where to buy them (operator table, 11 October 2026)
records.address: Tickets may be purchased onboard by cash or contactless; sales points and machines are listed by MPT
records.hours: Tickets are valid for two hours with free transfers inside that window. Missed-ticket penalty: €50. Explore Child 7-day is €7.00 (ages 4–10). Cards and singles are sold at the airport, the Valletta and Buġibba terminals and Sliema Ferries, and the page does not print the 2026/27 winter changeover date.
records.description: The operator’s fare page, read 11 October 2026, publishes a single ticket table and a separate card table. Singles bought from the driver with cash, a contactless bank card or a phone are €2.00 (winter) or €2.50 (summer) on day routes and are valid for two hours with free transfers. The 12 Single Day Journeys card costs €19.00 and is shareable between travellers; the Explore Flex card costs €21.00 for four days or €27.00 for seven days and its offer grid explicitly includes Day Routes, Night Routes, Airport Direct and Special Services; the separate Explore Adult 7-day card at €25.00 explicitly excludes tallinja Direct Routes. A €50 penalty applies to travellers who cannot show a valid ticket, and cards must be validated on boarding. The page states the winter €2.00 single-fare period as running from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026, which does not resolve which single fare applies during 13–19 October 2026.
records.notes: Fare page read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Card-sales locations and machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . TD1 Airport Direct detail: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/other-services/airport-direct/ . Worked comparison for a seven-day trip that includes airport days and daily event travel: Explore Flex 7-day €27.00 already includes Airport Direct, which would otherwise cost TD1 singles at €3.50 each way (€7.00 return); Explore Adult 7-day €25.00 plus two TD1 singles is about €32.00, and a 12-journey €19.00 card would be partly consumed by the two extra Airport Direct journeys. That comparison is arithmetic on published prices, not a quote, and assumes the traveller actually needs Airport Direct and daily buses. The page also sells Explore Flex bundle upgrades that add a Gozo Highspeed return (€42.00 for 7 days) or a harbour cruise (€42.00 for 7 days). Confirm activation, expiry and inclusions at a sales office before buying. Sales offices and ticket machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . The page states that the €2.00 winter fare applied from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026 and lists a separate summer day-route fare of €2.50, but it does not print the 2026/27 winter start date, so the exact seasonal boundary for this trip stays open. Recheck the day before travel, because seasonal prices and card inclusions change. Break-even arithmetic for this exact seven-day trip, and the €25 Explore Adult versus €27 Explore Flex comparison when Airport Direct is wanted, is worked out in the separate record trip-fare-scenarios-13-19-oct; the seasonal question is handled in mpt-seasonal-fare-window-2026 and sales points in mpt-card-sales-points.
records.price range: On-board/contactless single: €2.00 winter day route, €2.50 summer day route; night route €3.00; Special Service €3.00; tallinja Direct €3.00; TD1 €3.50. Cards: 12 Single Day Journeys €19.00 (shareable); Explore Flex 4-day €21.00 and 7-day €27.00 (both include Day, Night, Airport Direct and Special Services); Explore Adult 7-day €25.00 (excludes tallinja Direct Routes); Explore Child 7-day €7.00.

records.name: Event-day plan A — public bus Qawra → Ta’ Qali Stadium (Route 186)
records.address: Board at Qawra (952) / Luzzu (951) / Il-Qawra Arznell (950); alight at Ta’ Qali Stadium (6227)
records.hours: Outbound boards roughly 06:09–21:39 from Qawra 952, arriving Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227 about 30 minutes later, every 30 minutes. Return boards the opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 toward Buġibba; the operator’s grid shows a last listed 20:53 departure with a Buġibba Bay 1 arrival at 21:27.
records.description: Planning sequence for each event day. 1) Confirm on the organizer’s channels what time the doors actually open and close, because no TWC spectator schedule is published and a late playoff finish is the biggest risk. 2) Buy or top up a card that covers Day Routes — the €27.00 Explore Flex 7-day card is the only published card whose own offer grid explicitly includes Airport Direct, Night Routes and Special Services — or pay €2.50 per single on board if the summer fare still applies. 3) Ask the hotel front desk which Qawra stop side is correct and how long the walk is; Qawra 952, Luzzu 951 and Il-Qawra Arznell 950 are all listed on Route 186 within a few minutes of each other. 4) Board toward Rabat and alight at Ta’ Qali Stadium 6227. 5) For the return, cross to Stadium 2194 and board toward Buġibba, then connect onward to the hotel by a second bus or a short taxi hop, because that direction does not serve the Qawra seafront. 6) If the finish is after about 20:53, take a taxi or ride-hailing car instead — no night route serving Ta’ Qali or Ħ’Attard was found, and night routes were verified only from Buġibba (N212) and Valletta (N13).
records.notes: This is a planning sequence assembled from the operator’s own published grids and notices, not a verified door-to-door journey. Underlying sources: Route 186 stop grids https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ (read 11 October 2026); fares and card inclusions https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ ; service notices https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ ; night-route announcement https://www.publictransport.com.mt/new-night-routes/ ; date-specific planner https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Unverified pieces: the walk from each Qawra stop to AX ODYCY, the walk from Stadium 6227/2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate, the correct side of the road at each stop, and whether Route 186 runs to plan on the specific dates. The operator’s own Route 186 page also lists a Friday/Saturday evening diversion starting 17 October. Re-run the planner on the day and keep a live Bolt, eCabs, Uber or Malta Taxi quote as the fallback: https://bolt.eu/en/cities/malta/ , https://ecabs.com.mt/ , https://www.uber.com/global/en/r/cities/valletta-valletta-mt/ , https://www.maltataxi.mt/ . Session note: this plan and the records it cites were assembled across both 11 October verification sessions; where the two sessions differ, the more cautious figure is kept (static timetable spans are labelled as such, and the operator’s date-specific planner remains authoritative).
records.price range: €2.50 summer / €2.00 winter single per person per direction if the seasonal boundary falls where expected; €19.00 for 12 shareable journeys; €27.00 for a 7-day Explore Flex card that also covers Airport Direct, Night Routes and Special Services.

records.name: Getting back to Qawra after the event — the Route 186 return-leg transfer
records.address: Alight at the Route 186 terminus Buġibba Bay 1 (2527), or earlier in the Buġibba area, then board a Qawra-bound service. Stop sides and the walking distance between them are not verified.
records.hours: Last listed Route 186 departure from Ta' Qali Stadium 2194 toward Buġibba is 20:53, arriving Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) at about 21:26 in the variant traced. Onward Qawra-bound services from the Buġibba area are listed into the evening, but no specific dated connection was verified.
records.description: This is the most important transport constraint found for the event days. Route 186 toward Buġibba does not serve any Il-Qawra stop: its listed stops run from Rabat through Ta' Qali Stadium (2194), Mosta, Burmarrad and St Paul's Bay to a terminus at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). AX ODYCY is on the Qawra coast, so the return needs a second boarding. MPT's own page lists other routes at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) — 31, 31A, 45, 48, 203, 212, 214, 221, 223, 280, N48, N212, TD5 and TD13 — and at the Il-Qawra stops Arznell 950 / Luzzu 951 / Qawra 952 — 45, 212, 214, 221, 223, 280, N11, N212, TD1, TD13 and 406. The services appearing in both lists (45, 212, 214, 221, 223, 280, N212, TD13) are plausible onward options, but those lists mix both directions of each route and the two stops are on different sides of the Buġibba area, so a real connection must come from the dated MPT journey planner rather than be inferred here. Because the last listed Stadium 2194 departure is 20:53 and the playoff finish time is not published, keep a live-quote taxi or ride-hailing plan as the primary late-return option and treat the bus as the early-evening option.
records.notes: Stop chains and the "other routes operating from this bus stop" lists were read directly on 11 October 2026 from https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Two-hour transfer validity and the €50 no-ticket fine: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Night routes N212 (Buġibba) and N13 (Valletta) do not serve Ta' Qali: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/new-night-routes/ . Route 214 also connects the Buġibba/Qawra area with Ta' Qali Qali 2 (2542) and is worth comparing: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ . No dated connection, walk time, stop side, taxi quote or event finish time was verified, and the 17 October diversion may remove part of the return chain entirely.
records.price range: One single day fare covers the whole two-leg return, because MPT tickets are valid two hours with free transfers. At the unresolved October rate that is €2.00–€2.50 for both legs together, not each.

records.name: Bus cost scenarios for this exact trip (13–19 October, seven days)
records.area: Malta and Gozo — one traveller, seven-day window
records.address: Not applicable — arithmetic on published MPT prices
records.hours: Prices as published on the MPT fares page on 11 October 2026; they can change.
records.description: Arithmetic only, so the choice can be made in seconds once the real number of rides is known. At the conservative €2.50 single fare, break-even against the €19 12-journey card is 8 journeys (7 × €2.50 = €17.50; 8 × €2.50 = €20.00), and against the €25 Explore Adult 7-day card it is 10 journeys. At €2.00 the 12-journey card breaks even at 10 journeys and the €25 card at 13. A realistic event week — airport transfer, several Qawra or Valletta leisure trips, and four or five event-day round trips — will exceed 10 single journeys for most travellers, so an unlimited seven-day card is the likely better value, while the €19 shareable 12-journey card suits a couple taking only a few trips together. One caveat changes the answer: TD1 Airport Direct is €3.50 per single and is excluded from the €25 Explore Adult card according to that card's own paragraph, whereas the €27 Explore Flex 7-day explicitly includes Airport Direct. If you intend to use the airport bus, compare the €27 Flex. Which single fare actually applies in October is handled in the separate seasonal-window record, which reasons that on the operator's own published pattern the cheaper winter single begins after 19 October, making €2.50 the planning figure for this trip; that is a planning inference, not a published trip-week fare. None of this is a quote, a reservation, or a prediction of how often you will actually ride.
records.notes: Every price used here was read directly from https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ on 11 October 2026. The break-even figures are plain division of those published prices and assume each boarding is one journey; a two-leg return inside two hours counts as one fare because transfers are free. The October single-fare season is NOT established by the operator's page (its only dated winter window, 19 October 2025 – 13 June 2026, has expired), so both the €2.00 and €2.50 scenarios are shown. Card inclusions differ and are quoted from that page: Explore Flex unlimited offers include day routes, night routes, Airport Direct and special services; the Explore Adult 7-day paragraph excludes tallinja Direct routes. Confirm inclusions with MPT before buying. No traveller count, ride count, booking or reimbursement is assumed — enter your own figures in the expense planner. This record complements rather than repeats main-dataset records mpt-seasonal-fare-window-2026 (which fare applies), mpt-card-sales-points (where to buy) and mpt-fares-cards (the published table); it adds only the break-even arithmetic and the €25-versus-€27 Airport Direct comparison.
records.price range: Published inputs: single day fare €2.00 (winter) or €2.50 (summer), October season unresolved; 12 Single Day Journeys €19; Explore Adult 7-day €25; Explore Flex 7-day €27; Explore Flex 4-day €21; TD1 airport single €3.50.
